news.title: FIFA Plans Rule Change Following Controversial Balogun World Cup Suspension
news.lede: Rabat - FIFA is preparing to change its disciplinary rules following the controversy surrounding American striker Folarin Balogun, whose automatic suspension was lifted during the 2026 World Cup after US President Donald Trump contacted FIFA President Gianni Infantino. The proposed amendment would prevent automatic one-match suspensions from being suspended in similar circumstances, following criticism of FIFA's decision to allow Balogun to participate in the tournament's knockout stages. The issue was discussed during a FIFA Council meeting in Zurich on October 15, where officials agreed to review the disciplinary procedures involved in the case. According to the Royal Belgian Football Association (RBFA), FIFA has committed to amending Article 27 of its Disciplinary Code, with the proposed changes expected to be submitted for approval at the next Council meeting in Doha on December 16.

news.title: Morocco to Host 2027 Women’s World Cup Playoff Preliminary Round
news.lede: Rabat – The International Federation of Association Football (FIFA) has selected Morocco to host the preliminary round of the playoff tournament for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup, scheduled to take place from November 28 to December 5, 2026. According to FIFA’s official announcement , the matches will take place at the Mohammed VI Football Complex in Salé, near Rabat. Six national teams will participate in the competition: South Africa, Ghana, Ecuador, Uzbekistan, Chinese Taipei, and Papua New Guinea. The tournament will feature nine matches, with each team playing three games.

news.title: Infantino set to take his FIFA reelection campaign to Japan
news.lede: TOKYO — Gianni Infantino's campaign for reelection as FIFA president is set to move this week to Japan and a meeting scheduled for Wednesday with the Asian Football Confederation. This comes after Infantino apologized last week in Zurich, Switzerland, to FIFA's 37-member ruling council — which he chairs — for “mistakes” he made in assembling a now-scrapped $4.2 billion sell-off plan for the World Cup. The council is the main decision-making body at FIFA with a global spread of officials. The planned meeting with Asian soccer leaders is to be held in a five-star hotel in Tokyo with the media largely excluded.

news.title: Argentina striker’s double leaves New Zealand facing early World Cup exit
news.lede: New Zealand have suffered their second defeat at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco, losing 2-0 to Argentina in Group A. Argentinian striker Mercedes Diz scored both goals, striking either side of half-time to secure her country’s first victory of the tournament. The Argentinians created many first-half chances, hitting the crossbar three times with long-range efforts. Diz opened the scoring in the 42nd minute before adding her second in the 69th minute at the Mohammed VI Football Complex.

news.title: US under-17 women beat Samoa 17-0 for biggest win in World Cup history
news.lede: Result is largest margin at any age level of a World Cup. DiMaria is first to score six at Fifa finals since Haaland. Tournament is in year two of expanded 24-team field. The United States began their U-17 Women’s World Cup campaign on Monday with a record-setting 17-0 win over Samoa the biggest win at any age level in World Cup history.
